sites.intro: Each website gets its own Linux account and PHP processes, so one site cannot touch another.

redirects.title: Redirects
redirects.intro: Send visitors from one address to another, in the order listed.
redirects.aliases_hint: Visitors of the extra domains go to the same page on the main domain (301).

redirects.hint: From is a path such as /old-page, or a prefix such as /blog/* for everything under it. To is a path or a full address.

hotlink.title: Hotlink protection
hotlink.intro: Stop other websites from showing your images and media on their pages, using your bandwidth.
hotlink.extensions_hint: Separated by commas. Requests from pages of other sites get 403; direct visits still work.
hotlink.allowed_hint: One domain per line; *.example.com allows all its subdomains. This site's own domains always may.

php_settings.title: PHP settings
php_settings.intro: php.ini values for this site's PHP {{version}}. Empty fields use the default shown.

certificate.title: Own SSL certificate

php_ext.intro: Extensions of PHP {{version}} on this server, for every site using it. Locked ones are always installed.

server.title: Mail servers
server.intro: Each server with email runs its own mail server and webmail. Its host name is where mail apps connect and where other mail servers deliver.
server.enable_body: This installs a mail server (Stalwart) and webmail (Roundcube) and opens the mail ports in the firewall. It takes a minute or two.
server.hostname_hint: A name of its own, such as mail.example.com, pointing at this server. Webmail opens there too.
server.tls_auto: Let's Encrypt (the host name must point at this server)

sftp.intro: Use FileZilla, WinSCP or any SFTP app to manage this site's files. The account only sees this site's folder and cannot run commands.

sftp.keys_hint: Sign in without a password: paste public keys (id_ed25519.pub), one per line.

ftp.password_once: This FTP password is shown only now. Save it in your FTP program.

wordpress.title: Install WordPress
wordpress.intro: A fresh WordPress with its own MariaDB database, ready in about a minute. ekPanel creates the database, downloads WordPress, writes wp-config.php and sets up your admin account.
wordpress.installing: Installing WordPress. This takes about a minute; you can leave this page.
wordpress.failed: The last install did not finish: {{reason}}
wordpress.empty_note: The website folder must be empty (the ekPanel welcome page is fine), so none of your files are overwritten.
wordpress.password_once: Your WordPress admin password is shown only once. Copy it now; ekPanel does not keep it.
wordpress.installed_hint: Plugins and updates work directly from WordPress; no FTP details are needed.
wordpress.with_site_hint: Creates a database and installs WordPress as soon as the site is ready.

phpapps.title: Other applications
phpapps.intro: Install a content system, learning platform or framework into this empty website, with its own database.

about.joomla: Websites and portals with many extensions.
about.drupal: Structured content for larger sites (made with Composer).
about.moodle: Courses, quizzes and classes for schools and training.
about.laravel: A fresh Laravel app to build on (made with Composer).

phpapps.needs_php: Needs PHP {{version}} or newer; change the site's PHP version first.
phpapps.note: public_html must be empty. A database is made for {{name}}; installing takes a few minutes.
phpapps.installing: Installing {{name}}… this takes a few minutes.
phpapps.moodle_note: Moodle's background tasks run from a cron job every minute, added for you. Uploaded files are kept in moodledata, outside the website.
phpapps.laravel_note: Settings are in public_html/.env. Upload your code with SFTP or Git, then run its migrations from the terminal.

wptools.intro: Every WordPress site in one place: updates that undo themselves if they break the site, automatic update rules, hardening and staging copies. WordPress installed by hand is found too.
wptools.scan_started: Looking at every PHP website. New finds appear here in a moment.

empty.title: No WordPress sites yet
empty.body: Install WordPress on a website in one click, or look for WordPress you installed yourself.

running.update: Updating… the site is checked after each update.

outcome.rolled_back: broke the site, so the previous version was put back

auto.title: Automatic updates
auto.hint: ekPanel checks every day and updates by itself, checking the site after each update and undoing any that breaks it.

wptools.maintenance_hint: Visitors see a short "briefly unavailable" page; you can still sign in.
wptools.debug_on: Debug mode (WP_DEBUG) is on. Turn it off on a live site: it can show errors to visitors.

hardening.title: Hardening
hardening.hint: Common protections that do not change how the site works for visitors.
hardening.file_edit: No editing of plugin and theme code from the dashboard
hardening.file_edit_hint: A stolen admin password then cannot be used to add code.
hardening.xmlrpc_hint: An old remote interface used for password guessing. The block editor and apps using the REST API keep working.
hardening.uploads: No PHP in the uploads folder
hardening.uploads_hint: Only media belongs there; a script uploaded through a weak plugin cannot run.
hardening.loose_one: {{count}} file or folder others could change
hardening.loose_other: {{count}} files or folders others could change

staging.title: Staging
staging.hint: A private copy at {{domain}} to try changes on, with its own files and database. Search engines are asked not to index it.
staging.is_copy: This site is a staging copy. When it looks right, push it to the live site.
staging.push_title: Push the staging copy to the live site?
staging.push_body: The live site gets the staging copy's files and/or database. Its addresses are changed back to the live domain. The live site shows a maintenance page while copying.
staging.pull_title: Refresh the staging copy from the live site?
staging.pull_body: The staging copy gets the live site's current files and/or database. Changes made only on staging are replaced.
staging.files_hint: Plugins, themes, uploads and WordPress itself. The target keeps its wp-config.php.
staging.database_hint: Posts, pages, settings, users and orders.
staging.kept: Before overwriting, the target's database is saved, and replaced files are kept aside, in its tmp folder.

serversec.intro: CrowdSec detects and bans attacks, ClamAV looks for malware in the websites, and whole countries can be blocked. The checklist shows what else to tighten.

overview.title: Checklist
overview.firewall_off: The firewall is off: every port that a program opens is reachable.
overview.open_firewall: Turn it on on the server's page
overview.crowdsec_on_one: CrowdSec is running; {{count}} address banned now.
overview.crowdsec_on_other: CrowdSec is running; {{count}} addresses banned now.
overview.crowdsec_off: CrowdSec is off: password guessing and scans are not banned.
overview.root_ok: root cannot sign in over SSH with a password.
overview.root_password: root may sign in over SSH with a password (PermitRootLogin {{value}}). Use keys and set it to prohibit-password.
overview.password_on: SSH accepts passwords (port {{ports}}). Keys are safer; CrowdSec bans guessers meanwhile.
overview.updates_none: All packages are up to date.
overview.lists_old: The package lists are {{hours}} hours old.
overview.auto_off: Security updates are not installed automatically.
overview.reboot: Updates wait for a restart of the server.
overview.twofa_ok: Every administrator signs in with two-factor authentication.
overview.twofa_missing_one: {{count}} administrator signs in with a password only:
overview.twofa_missing_other: {{count}} administrators sign in with a password only:

malware.title: Malware scans
malware.intro: ClamAV scans the files of every website for viruses, web shells and other malware. Its virus database updates by itself.
malware.low_memory: This server has less than 2 GB of memory. ClamAV needs about 1.5 GB while it scans, so scans may fail; add memory or swap.
malware.site_intro: The malware scan found these files in this website. Delete them, or move them into quarantine, where they cannot run. Then find how they got in: outdated plugins and themes, or a leaked password.
malware.delete_confirm: Delete {{path}} for good? This cannot be undone.

crowdsec.intro: Reads SSH and web server logs, bans addresses that guess passwords, scan for weaknesses or try known exploits (also on WordPress), and blocks addresses its community reports. Bans are made in the firewall.
crowdsec.bouncer_down: The firewall part of CrowdSec is not running, so bans have no effect. Restart crowdsec-firewall-bouncer on the server's page.
crowdsec.cloudflare_note: Visitors through Cloudflare's proxy reach the server from Cloudflare's addresses, which are never banned; their attacks are logged and banned for direct access only. Block them at Cloudflare too.

countries.title: Country blocking
countries.intro: Drops connections by the country of their address, for everything on this server: websites, SSH, email and FTP.
countries.m_allow_hint: Every other country is blocked. Make sure the countries you and your visitors connect from are on the list.
countries.blocks_you: This would block you: your address {{ip}} is in {{country}}. Add it to the allowlist first.
countries.notes: Port 80 stays open so certificates can renew; it only redirects to HTTPS. The allowlist and this server's own, Cloudflare's and private addresses are never blocked, so visitors through Cloudflare's proxy are not blocked here: block them at Cloudflare.

bans.title: Banned addresses
bans.intro: Detected attackers and addresses banned by hand. The community's list is not shown.
bans.allowlisted: {{ip}} is on the allowlist. Remove it there first.

alerts.title: Recent attacks
alerts.intro: What CrowdSec detected on this server.

allowlist.title: Allowlist
allowlist.intro: Addresses and networks never banned or blocked by country, such as your office. One per line.
allowlist.always: Always allowed as well: this server's and Cloudflare's addresses ({{count}})

backups.intro: Encrypted, deduplicated backups of your websites and databases, kept on the server or in S3-compatible storage.

empty.title: No backups yet
empty.body: Add a backup location and ekPanel backs up every website and database on that server on a schedule.

kind_hint.local: Fast to set up, but lost if the server's disk is lost.
kind_hint.s3: Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, MinIO and others. Safer: kept off the server.

backups.name: Name

s3.endpoint_hint: The host name only, for example s3.us-west-002.backblazeb2.com
s3.secret_note: The keys are stored only on the server, readable by root. The panel does not keep them.

backups.keep_hint: Older backups are removed after each run. Because backups are deduplicated, keeping many costs little extra space.
backups.connect_existing: Connect backups made earlier, using their recovery key
backups.recovery_once: This is the recovery key. It is shown only this once. Without it, nobody (including you) can read these backups.
backups.recovery_hint: Keep it somewhere safe and away from this server, such as a password manager. You need it to restore after rebuilding the server.
backups.no_snapshots: No backups here yet. Click “Back up now” to make the first one.

mode_hint.folder: Puts the files in a “restored-…” folder in the site's home, next to public_html. Nothing current changes.
mode_hint.replace: Swaps public_html for the backup. The current files move to the site's trash, so you can still get them back.

backups.db_restore_warning: This replaces everything in the database with the backup. Changes made since then are lost.
backups.remove_body: Stops backing up here. The backups themselves are not deleted; you can connect them again with the recovery key.
backups.remove_confirm: ekPanel stops backing up here and forgets the location. The stored backups stay where they are and can be connected again with the recovery key.
backups.saved_it: I have saved the recovery key
backups.remove_body_local: Stops backing up here. The backups already made stay on the server in {{path}}; delete that folder yourself if you no longer need them.
backups.remove_confirm_local: ekPanel stops backing up here and forgets the location. The backups stay in {{path}} on the server, and cannot be connected again from the panel.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.unmanaged: ekPanel is not managing this server's firewall, so whatever firewall the server has stays as it is. Turn it on to block every incoming connection except SSH, websites, the ekPanel agent and the ports you open.
firewall.off: The firewall is off: every port that a program listens on can be reached. Your rules are kept for when you turn it on again.
firewall.always_open: Always open: SSH ({{ssh}}), HTTP (80), HTTPS (443) and the ekPanel agent (7443). Everything else coming in is blocked unless a rule below opens it.
firewall.confirm_on: Incoming connections are blocked except SSH ({{ssh}}), HTTP, HTTPS and the ekPanel agent. Anything else that is reached from outside (a mail server, a game server, a database used by other machines) stops working until you open its port.
firewall.confirm_off: Every port that a program listens on becomes reachable from the internet.

apps.intro: Run any Docker image or Compose file. Ports stay private to the server; a domain with free HTTPS points at the app.

empty.title: Run your first app
empty.body: Install a ready-made service from the catalogue, run any Docker image, or paste a Compose file. ekPanel installs Docker on first use.

kind_hint.image: One container from an image, with variables and kept folders.
kind_hint.compose: Several services described in a docker-compose.yml.
kind_hint.git: Built from a branch with its Dockerfile, released without downtime.

apps.name: Name
apps.name_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Used for the folder and containers.
apps.image_hint: From Docker Hub or any registry, for example nginx:alpine or ghcr.io/owner/app:1.2
apps.compose_hint: Ports are kept private: publish them on 127.0.0.1, or use the port setting below for the domain.
apps.service_hint: The service in the Compose file that listens on the port.

apps.first_run: The first app on a server installs Docker, which takes a minute or two. Images download on the server.
apps.not_ready: Setting up the app on the server…
apps.no_containers: No containers. If the app is stopped, start it.

delete.title: Delete this app
delete.body: Stops and removes its containers. You choose whether its data goes too.

delete.with_data_hint: Removes the volumes and /srv/ekpanel/apps/{{name}}. This cannot be undone.

catalog.title: App catalogue
catalog.intro: Ready-made services, reviewed by ekPanel. Passwords and keys are made fresh for every install.
catalog.browse: install a ready-made service from the catalogue
catalog.none_body: Try another word, or run any image with Add app.
catalog.no_servers: Add a server first; services are installed on one of your servers.
catalog.domain_hint: The service is used through this domain. Point its DNS at the server first; HTTPS is set up for it.

catalog.what_runs: What will run, and a memory limit
catalog.memory_hint: Optional, for the main service. It needs about {{size}} MB.
catalog.sign_in_hint: These are the app's variables. Changing a password in the app itself does not change them here.
catalog.compose_fixed: The Compose file and port come from the catalogue. You can change the domain, variables and limits.

uptime-kuma.description: Watch websites, servers and services, and get alerts when they go down.
uptime-kuma.notes: Open the app right after installing: the first visitor creates the administrator account.

grafana.description: Dashboards and charts for metrics and logs from many data sources.
grafana.notes: Sign in with the user name and password below.

n8n.description: Automate work by connecting apps and APIs in a visual workflow editor.
n8n.notes: Open the app right after installing to create the owner account. Keep N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY: credentials saved in n8n cannot be read without it.

gitea.description: Light Git hosting with pull requests, issues, wikis and a package registry.
gitea.notes: Open the app right after installing and finish the setup page, where you create the administrator account. Git works over HTTPS.

it-tools.description: Handy tools for developers in one place: converters, generators, formatters and more.

vaultwarden.description: A light password manager that works with the Bitwarden apps and browser extensions.
vaultwarden.notes: Create your account, then set SIGNUPS_ALLOWED to false in the variables so nobody else can sign up. The admin page at /admin asks for the token below.

umami.description: Simple website analytics that respects privacy and needs no cookies.
umami.notes: Sign in as admin with the password umami, and change it right away.

ghost.description: A publishing platform for blogs, newsletters and paid memberships.
ghost.notes: The first start takes a minute or two while the database is set up. Then open /ghost on the domain to create the owner account. Newsletters need a mail service, set up in Ghost.

listmonk.description: Newsletters and mailing lists, with templates, fast sending and reports.
listmonk.notes: Sign in with the user name and password below. Add your SMTP server in Settings → SMTP to send mail.

nextcloud.description: Your own cloud for files, calendars and contacts, with apps for every device.
nextcloud.notes: Sign in with the user name and password below. The first start takes a few minutes while Nextcloud sets itself up.

memos.description: Quick notes and a personal timeline, written in Markdown.
memos.notes: Open the app right after installing: the first account becomes the administrator.

excalidraw.description: A whiteboard for sketching diagrams that look hand-drawn.
excalidraw.notes: Drawings stay in the browser. Use Export to save them as files.

ntfy.description: Send push notifications to your phone or computer from scripts and apps.
ntfy.notes: Nobody can use it until you add a user: open the app's shell and run ntfy user add --role=admin yourname

redis.description: A fast in-memory store for caches, sessions and queues, for websites and apps on this server.
redis.notes: Connect to 127.0.0.1:{{port}} with the password below. It cannot be reached from other servers.

deploys.title: Deployments
deploys.repo_hint: Its https:// address, or for a private repository its SSH address (git@github.com:owner/app.git) with the deploy key the app page shows.
deploys.context_hint: The folder Docker builds from; . is the whole repository.
deploys.port_hint: The port the app listens on inside its container. Needed to release without downtime.
deploys.env_hint: One NAME=value per line. The Dockerfile can also read them while building, with ARG NAME.
deploys.auto_hint: When the repository's webhook reports a push to the branch, build and release it.
deploys.webhook_hint: In the repository's settings, add a webhook with this address and secret, for push events, sending JSON. Works with GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo.
deploys.deploy_key_hint: Add this key to the repository as a read-only deploy key, so the server can clone it over SSH.
deploys.deploy_key_https: Needed only for private repositories: switch the address to SSH and add this key to the repository as a read-only deploy key.
deploys.none: Nothing deployed yet. Deploy builds the branch with its Dockerfile and starts it.
deploys.waiting: Waiting for the build to start…

builder_hint.auto: The Dockerfile if the repository has one, otherwise Railpack.
builder_hint.railpack: Detects the language and framework; no Dockerfile needed.

issue.conflict: is already used ({{have}}); ekPanel would set {{want}}.

dns.name_hint: www, @ for {{zone}} itself, or a full name in the zone.

dns.cloudflare_intro: Domains at Cloudflare, kept in sync with your websites and apps.

hosted.title: ekPanel name servers

hosted.none: No domains on ekPanel's name servers yet.

tpl.delete_confirm: Delete the template {{name}}? Domains made with it keep their records.

hosted.zone_intro: On ekPanel's own name servers. Records for websites, apps and email on this domain are made by ekPanel.
hosted.delete_confirm: Remove {{name}} from ekPanel's name servers? Its records stop being answered there.

previews.none: No open pull requests. Open one in the repository to see its preview here.
previews.goes_away: It is removed when the pull request closes.

customers.intro: People who host with you. Each customer sees only their own websites, databases and apps, within the limits of their package.

empty.title: No customers yet
empty.body: Create a package first, then add customers. They sign in to this panel with their own account.

customers.needs_package: Create a package before adding customers.
customers.password_generated: A password is generated and shown once. You can reset it later.
customers.password_once: The customer's password, shown only this once. Send it to them over a safe channel.
customers.share_hint: They can change it under Security after signing in.
customers.delete_body: The account is removed. A customer who still owns something cannot be deleted.
customers.delete_has: They still have {{sites}} websites, {{databases}} databases and {{apps}} apps. Delete or move them first.
customers.acting_as: You are signed in as {{name}} ({{email}}). Everything you do is recorded under your own name.

move.title: Move {{name}}'s things
move.intro: Move everything this customer has on one server (websites, databases and apps) to another, one after the other. Their first website takes all their databases there along. If something fails, the move stops; what moved stays moved.
move.warning: Apps are unavailable while they move, and changes made to websites after their copy starts are not carried over. Each old copy stays until you remove it from the website's, database's or app's page.
move.started: The move has started. Each website, database and app shows its progress on its own page, where you can also remove its old copy once it has moved.

customers.reset_2fa_confirm: Turn off two-factor sign-in for {{name}}? They sign in with their password and can turn it on again. Do this only when you know it is really them.

packages.intro: What each customer may use: how many websites, databases and apps, disk space, and memory and CPU for all their processes together.

empty.title: No packages yet
empty.body: A package sets a customer's limits. Make one, such as "Starter" or "Business", then add customers to it.

packages.name: Name
packages.counts_hint: How many of each a customer may have. 0 for apps means no Docker apps.
packages.limits_hint: Memory and CPU cover all of a customer's PHP and app processes together. Empty means no limit.
packages.servers_hint: Where the customer may create things. None ticked means every server.
packages.images_hint: One per line: a name such as nginx (any tag), or a prefix ending in / such as ghcr.io/acme/. Empty means any image. Customers cannot use Compose files.
packages.git_apps_hint: Customers can build and deploy their own repositories. Builds run on the server, within the package's memory and CPU.
packages.mailbox_size_hint: Largest size of one mailbox. Leave empty for no limit.

cron.title: Cron jobs
cron.none: No scheduled jobs. Add one to run a command on a schedule, such as a backup script or a Laravel scheduler.
cron.command_hint_site: Runs with sh as the website's own account, starting in public_html. Output is kept in the job's log.
cron.command_hint_app: Runs with sh inside the app's container.
cron.expression_hint: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example 30 2 * * 1-5
cron.name: Name (optional)
cron.service_hint: The app's service to run in. Image apps have one, app.

traffic.title: Traffic
traffic.none: No requests in this time range yet.
traffic.delay: Counted from the web server's log every 15 minutes.

weblogs.title: Logs
weblogs.php_empty: No PHP errors logged. Errors from your code show up here.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty: Nothing yet. Alerts about your servers, websites and backups appear here.
notifications.intro: Choose where alerts go: email, Telegram, Discord, Slack or a webhook. They always appear under the bell too.
notifications.no_channels: No channels yet. Alerts still appear under the bell.
notifications.name: Name
notifications.chat_id_hint: Your chat's number (ask @userinfobot) or a channel's @name. Send /start to the bot first.

url_hint.discord: Server settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy URL.
url_hint.slack: An Incoming Webhook URL from your Slack app.
url_hint.webhook: ekPanel sends a signed JSON POST to this address.

notifications.keep_secret: Leave empty to keep the saved one.
notifications.key_once: The signing key, shown only this once. Check the X-Ekpanel-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body) with it.
notifications.key_hint: Keep it in the service that receives the webhook.

mail.title: Mail server and panel address
mail.body: Email notifications go out through this SMTP server. The panel address makes the links in messages work.
mail.panel_url_hint: How people open this panel, such as https://panel.example.com

terminal.confirm_body: A terminal can change anything on the server. Confirm it is you; this lasts 15 minutes.
terminal.note: Opening and closing are recorded in the audit log. The shell closes after 30 minutes without typing.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: Keep the panel and the agent on every server up to date. Releases are signed; the panel checks the signature before installing anything.
updates.not_release: This panel is built from source, not from a release, so it does not update itself. Install a release to get updates.
updates.never_checked: Not checked yet. The panel looks for new releases every 6 hours.
updates.check_off: Automatic checks are turned off (EKPANEL_UPDATE_CHECK=false). You can still check by hand.

steps.download: The agent on this server downloads the release and checks its signature.
steps.backup: It saves a copy of the panel's database in /var/backups/ekpanel.
steps.restart: It installs the new panel and restarts it. The panel is away for a few seconds; if the new version does not start, the previous one is put back.
steps.agents: The new panel then updates the agent on each server, one at a time. Websites keep running throughout.

updates.confirm: Update ekPanel to {{version}}? The panel restarts during the update.
updates.panel_agent_offline: The agent on the panel's own server is not connected, so it cannot install the update.
updates.restarting: The panel is restarting. This page continues by itself.
updates.reload_hint: The panel now runs {{version}}. Reload the page to use the new version of this interface.
updates.backup: Database copy taken before the update: {{path}}

agents.title: Agents
agents.body: Each server's agent should run the same version as the panel. A server that was offline during an update can be updated here later.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: Tokens let scripts and the ekctl command-line tool use the panel's API as you. Give each one only the scopes it needs.
tokens.empty_hint: Make one for each script or computer, so you can revoke it on its own.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.name_hint: What uses it, such as "Laptop" or "Deploy script".
tokens.revoke_confirm: Revoke the token "{{name}}"? Anything that uses it stops working at once.
tokens.created_once: Copy it now and keep it somewhere safe. It is shown only this once; the panel keeps only a fingerprint of it.
tokens.never_with_token: A token can never change your password, two-factor sign-in or tokens, and cannot open a terminal.
tokens.how_body: Send it in the Authorization header:
tokens.how_cli: Or sign in with the ekctl command-line tool: ekctl login --url followed by this panel's address.

scope_hint.read: See everything you can see in the panel, but change nothing.
scope_hint.sites: Websites, WordPress, PHP apps and cron jobs.
scope_hint.apps: Docker apps, deploys and the app catalogue.
scope_hint.servers: Servers, their services, firewall and security.
scope_hint.settings: Panel settings, updates, notifications and the audit log.

move.title: Move to another server
move.intro: Copy this website (files, chosen databases and certificate) from {{server}} to another server. The old copy keeps serving until you remove it.
move.no_databases: No databases of this website's owner on its server.
move.databases_hint: They keep their names, users and passwords, so the website's settings stay right.
move.step_copy: The files, databases and certificate are copied straight from server to server.
move.step_switch: The new server sets it up, and it is checked. If anything fails, it stays where it is.
move.step_dns: DNS records the panel manages point to the new server by themselves; otherwise you change them.
move.step_cleanup: The old copy keeps serving until you remove it.
move.writes_warning: Changes made on the old copy after the copy starts (new orders, comments, uploads) are not carried over. Move at a quiet time.
move.moved: The website now runs on {{to}}. The old copy on {{from}} still answers visitors whose DNS has not changed yet.
move.dns_hint: If the panel does not manage this domain's DNS, point its records to {{ip}} now.
move.dns_hint_noip: If the panel does not manage this domain's DNS, point its records to the new server now.
move.cleanup_confirm: Remove the old copy on {{server}}? Its files and databases there are deleted. Only do this once the domain points to the new server.
move.intro_app: Copy this app (its data volumes and, for a Git app, its current build) from {{server}} to another server.
move.moved_app: The app now runs on {{to}}. The old copy on {{from}} is stopped and keeps its data until you remove it.
move.step_copy_app: The app is stopped, then its data and (for a Git app) its build are copied straight from server to server.
move.step_cleanup_app: The old copy stays stopped, with its data, until you remove it.
move.app_warning: The app is unavailable from the moment it stops until it runs on the new server and its domain points there.
move.cleanup_confirm_app: Remove the old copy on {{server}}? Its containers and data there are deleted. Only do this once the app works on the new server and its domain points there.
move.intro_database: Copy this database (its data, users and password) from {{server}} to another server.
move.moved_database: The database now runs on {{to}}. The old copy on {{from}} stays until you remove it.
move.step_copy_database: The database is dumped and loaded straight from server to server.
move.step_cleanup_database: The old copy stays until you remove it.
move.cleanup_confirm_database: Remove the old copy of the database on {{server}}? It is deleted there. Only do this once nothing uses it any more.
move.database_warning: Websites and apps on the old server connect to the database there and keep using the old copy, and changes made to it after the copy starts are not carried over. To move a website with its database, move the website instead.
move.in_use_confirm: These are still on the old server and may use the old copies of the databases: {{users}}. Removing the old copy breaks them if they do. Remove it anyway?

rebuild.title: Rebuild {{domain}} from a backup
rebuild.offline: {{server}} is offline. If it is gone, rebuild this website on another server from its newest backup.
rebuild.intro: The website and the databases you choose are set up on the new server and filled from their newest snapshots in a backup storage connected there. Nothing is copied from the old server.
rebuild.repo: Backup storage on the new server
rebuild.no_repo: Connect the same S3 storage on the new server first (Backups → Add backup location, with its recovery key).
rebuild.warning: Everything since the newest backup is lost. If the old server comes back, its copy stays until you remove it from this page.

imports.title: Import
imports.description: Bring websites over from another host: a whole cPanel account from its backup, or one website from an archive of its files (aaPanel, any host, plain WordPress).
imports.step_upload: 1. Put the backup on a server
imports.upload_body: In cPanel, make a full account backup (or ask the host for the cpmove file). Copy it to {{dir}} on the server that will host the websites, then enter its file name here.
imports.reading: Reading the backup. A large one can take a few minutes.
imports.no_databases: The backup has no MySQL databases.
imports.cron_hint: They run as the main website's account, with the website's PHP version. Paths in /home/{{user}}/ change to the new home folder.
imports.cron_needs_main: Cron jobs go to the main website: choose it to import them.
imports.not_certs: Certificates: new ones are issued once the domains point here.
imports.running_body: Everything chosen is being set up, then the files, data and mail are copied in. You can leave this page; the import goes on.
imports.failed_body: Websites, databases, mail domains and DNS zones the panel made for it are still listed. Delete them before you try again.
imports.new_passwords: These databases have new passwords: {{names}}. Set the new password in the website's configuration (on the database's page).
imports.after: Check each website (for example with an entry in your computer's hosts file), then point the domains at this server: change their name servers to ekPanel's if you imported the zones, or their records at your DNS host. Certificates are issued once the domains point here.
imports.paths_changed_one: The old home folder's path was changed in {{count}} file
imports.paths_changed_other: The old home folder's path was changed in {{count}} files

note.certificate: Certificate of {{name}}: a new one is issued once the domain points here
note.links_outside_one: {{count}} link that points outside the website
note.links_outside_other: {{count}} links that point outside the website
note.db_user: Database user {{name}} for {{detail}}: here a database has a user of its own, now {{detail}}
note.cron_line: Cron job that could not be read: {{name}}
note.cron_no_main_one: {{count}} cron job: it belongs to the main website, which was not imported
note.cron_no_main_other: {{count}} cron jobs: they belong to the main website, which was not imported
note.mail_mailbox: Mailbox {{name}}: its name cannot be used here
note.mail_forwarder: Forwarding of {{name}}: an address it forwards to cannot be used here
note.mail_mdbox: Mail of {{name}}: kept in Dovecot's mdbox format, which cannot be read. The mailbox is made, empty; move the mail with a mail program or imapsync
note.zone_mx_here: Zone {{name}}: its MX record points at {{detail}}, which now points here, where it has no email. Import the email too, or change the MX record
note.zone_old_ip: Records that still point at the old server ({{detail}}): {{name}}
note.zone_record: Record of {{detail}} that ekPanel cannot keep: {{name}}
note.zone_unread_one: Zone {{name}}: {{count}} line of its file could not be read
note.zone_unread_other: Zone {{name}}: {{count}} lines of its file could not be read
note.mail_unusable: Forwarding line of {{detail}}: {{name}} (to a program or a refusal, which ekPanel does not have)
note.mail_catch_all: Catch-all of {{detail}}: unknown addresses went to {{name}}, which is not a mailbox here; choose a mailbox on the domain's Email page
note.outside_website_one: {{count}} file outside the website's folder in the archive
note.outside_website_other: {{count}} files outside the website's folder in the archive
note.dump_unused: Database dump {{name}}: no database was made for it
note.open_basedir: open_basedir in .user.ini (it named the old server's folder; PHP here limits the website itself)
note.dumps_one: {{count}} database dump in the website's folder (it could have been downloaded)
note.dumps_other: {{count}} database dumps in the website's folder (they could have been downloaded)
note.coolify_env_hidden_one: {{count}} variable came without its value: the token may not read sensitive data. Fill it in on the app's page
note.coolify_env_hidden_other: {{count}} variables came without their values: the token may not read sensitive data. Fill them in on the app's page
note.coolify_volumes_one: {{count}} volume: the folder is kept here, empty. Copy its data from Coolify's server
note.coolify_volumes_other: {{count}} volumes: the folders are kept here, empty. Copy their data from Coolify's server
note.coolify_files_one: {{count}} file mount from Coolify is not imported
note.coolify_files_other: {{count}} file mounts from Coolify are not imported
note.coolify_more_domains: More domains ({{name}}): an app here has one domain; point the others at it with a redirect or another app
note.coolify_no_port: The domain {{name}} has no port to route to: add the domain and the container port on the app's page
note.coolify_builder: Built with Railpack here (Coolify used {{name}}): check the first build
note.coolify_deploy_key: A private repository: add the app's deploy key (on its page) to the repository, then deploy
note.coolify_deploy: Nothing runs yet: deploy it from the app's page to build the first release
note.coolify_github_app: {{name}} came through Coolify's GitHub App: if it is private, change it to its SSH address (git@github.com:owner/repo.git) and add the app's deploy key to the repository

imports.mail_off: This server has no email. Turn on email for it (Email → Servers) to import mailboxes.
imports.zones_hint: Made on ekPanel's name servers. Records for the websites and email here are made by ekPanel; cPanel's own names are left out; everything else is kept.
imports.zones_off: ekPanel's name servers are not set up (DNS → Name servers), so zones cannot be imported. Keep them at your DNS host.
imports.new_mail_passwords: These mailboxes have new passwords: {{names}}. Set a password on each one's page and tell its user.

mode.cpanel_hint: A whole account: websites, databases, email, cron jobs, DNS
mode.archive_hint: One website from a .zip or .tar.gz, with its database dump
mode.coolify_hint: Applications and services, through Coolify's API

imports.archive_body: Copy the website's files as one .zip, .tar.gz or .tar to {{dir}} on the server, and its database dump (.sql or .sql.gz) next to it if it has one. aaPanel's site and database backups work as they are.
imports.archive_choose: 2. Choose how to set it up
imports.domain_taken: Another website or app here uses this domain.
imports.wp_keeps: WordPress keeps its database password: the database is made with it, and wp-config.php gets the name and user below and localhost.
imports.wp_new_password: wp-config.php has no database password, so the database gets a new one: put it in wp-config.php.
imports.db_hint: The database gets a new password, shown once when the import starts: put it in the website's settings.
imports.db_taken_rename: This server already has a database or user with this name: choose another; wp-config.php will get it.
imports.wp_address: WordPress keeps its address from its database: import it under the same domain, or change the address afterwards (Settings → General).
imports.db_password_once: The database's password, shown only now:
imports.step_upload_archive: 1. Put the archive on a server
imports.coolify_body: In Coolify, open Keys & Tokens → API tokens and make a token that may read (with read:sensitive, so variables come with their values). The token is used for this import only and is not kept.
imports.coolify_empty: Coolify has no applications or services.

coolify_reason.database: Databases are not imported: make one here and load a dump of it
coolify_reason.build_pack: This kind of build cannot be imported
coolify_reason.no_compose: Coolify did not send its Compose file: the token needs read:sensitive

imports.coolify_data: Settings come over: image, Compose file or Git repository, the first domain and its port, variables and the folders kept in volumes. The data in the volumes does not: copy it yourself before you point the domains here.
imports.coolify_after: The apps start on the server now. Copy their data, check them, then point their domains at this server.
